mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) within the next 6 months, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings signal from accelerating GDP.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, as measured by the year-over-year change in the INDPRO index, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a sharp INDPRO drop, indicating the supply shock is not reliably negative for equities.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate, defined as an increase of > 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months, signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises > 5 points in the month following the UNRATE trigger, indicating the labor market weakening is not negatively impacting consumer psyche.

mechanism_narrative: An inverted yield curve, defined as the 10-year Treasury yield falling below the 2-year yield, signals a looming recession that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX posts positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances following a yield curve inversion, indicating the inversion is not a reliable recession signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in housing starts, as measured by the year-over-year change in the HOUST index, signals a weakening housing market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Homebuilder stocks (ITB ETF) outperform the S&P 500 by > 5% in the 20 days following the HOUST drop, indicating the housing market weakness is not broadly negative for equities.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate, defined as a rise of > 1 percentage point over the past 3 months, signals a tightening monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: High-yield corporate bond spreads (BofA index) narrow by > 50 bps in the month following the FEDFUNDS trigger, indicating the rate hike is not negatively impacting credit markets.

mechanism_narrative: An accelerating pace of job growth, as measured by the 3-month moving average of the year-over-year change in PAYEMS, signals a strengthening labor market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims (ICSA) rise by > 10% in the month following the PAYEMS acceleration, indicating the labor market strength is not sustainable.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in consumer prices, as measured by the year-over-year change in the CPI index, signals an overheating economy that will prompt a monetary policy tightening, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed pauses its rate hiking cycle within 3 months of the CPI trigger, indicating the inflation signal is not prompting the expected policy tightening.
